prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on growth: profit grew 50% compared with a year earlier. Also in its favour: sales grew 23% compared with a year earlier; over the past year the share did 0.3 percentage points better than the Nifty 50; and the share price is close to its 52-week high. Other areas on this side: the recent price trend, cash flow and the balance sheet.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated. Also against it: return on capital employed is only 7.3%, a weak return on the money in the business; net debt is 6.4 times a year of operating earnings, heavy; and operating profit covers interest only 1.4 times, thin. Other areas on this side: the balance sheet, the recent price trend, what the price implies.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 5 points in favour and 9 against give more points against. The pool score is 46 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
